title: #497: Our Prerelease Guide for Reality Fracture
scale: No grades on air; the hosts graded commons and uncommons privately and instead give ranked top-three uncommon lists, notable commons, and sleepers per color.

cards.take: The buzziest card of the preview season, with rare-level power; red-green ramp can land it on turn five or six.
Agrees it is busted and wonders whether enough Heartwood tokens let you splash its heavy RRGG cost.
White's best two-drop: an evasive body that protects planeswalkers and grants flying to countered creatures, which is a lot for two mana.
Has it third and is fine with it being Ben's top pick.
A five-mana 4/4 flyer that makes Thopters off surveil; best cast when a Jace is ready to downtick, but still a decent Air Elemental otherwise.
Calls it busted when you can pair it with a Jace downtick on the same turn.
An interesting flash protection-and-counter twist, but he later bumped it from his top three.
The evasive 1/3 can bounce your own Way enchantments to re-empower Jace, which opens lots of cool lines.
Likes Ben's case for replaying Ways with it.
Good instant removal plus surveil, though being unable to hit two-drops may sting in a board-presence format.
Its floor of two Cadets plus surveils is Imperial Oath-adjacent, and Empower Jace is spread widely enough to play it in white.
Sees it as more of a card for green's Jace decks than for white.
Clearly strong removal that exiles any nonland permanent.
On his notable commons list as quality white removal.
Recalls Murdock's Crusade: flexible removal for big creatures that can also cycle and gain life.
A good card that only missed his list because white is so deep.
A 2/4 flying vigilance four-drop whose Seed Suture makes it a 3/4 later; absurdly good, and his whole white ranking leans on it.
Much better than the similar Gollum's Bite adventure creature; he has it as a sleeper.
An Imperial Oath-style three Cadets plus Empower Jace, with land cycling as a backup; predictably strong.
Wary of land cyclers, but this one is an exception because it still does its job.
A Pridemate-style two-drop that will just trade in combat; bad news for white's life gain plan.
The white two-drop he actually wants: a 3/1 that can later exile itself to Empower Jace 2.
White's good two-drop, balancing out the weak Hortimancer.
Likes it as a 2/3 flyer that can pump the team late; +1/+1 counter synergies otherwise look like a red herring.
A three-mana body that Empowers Jace 4; possibly the best common, and even better with Kiora in blue-green.
Just busted: sorcery-speed top-or-bottom removal plus an ongoing Empower Jace engine, with no build-around work needed.
Also his top blue uncommon.
A two-drop that does everything: evasion enabler, build-around potential, and high toughness to protect Jace.
A 1/5 flying vigilance prowess body that often costs two and feels like cheating; four mana is fine too.
Rules, and it's cube-bound; one of the high-toughness flying vigilance blockers that will make boards hard to attack.
Stands by last week's take: a cheap counterspell that also Empowers Jace.
Essence Scatter-plus, since it can also hit legendary Ways or shrink a creature, despite others' skepticism.
Agrees it's good.
The format's constant surveils turn off its defender, so it protects your Jace and attacks theirs; outstanding in blue-white.
Also on his sleeper list; a two-drop that will just be good.
A cheap evasive menace threat that recurs itself, is free value when milled, and fits deathtouch themes.
An instant edict that takes the opponent's biggest threat and gains life.
Empower Jace 5 plus a sac-for-4/4 ability; curving a Ravenous Rats-type into it is nasty.
Excellent cheap instant removal.
Banger instant exile removal, but splashable, which doesn't help black as a main color.
One of black's few exciting creatures: a 1/4 flyer that pressures Jaces, protects yours, and attacks over high-toughness boards.
Not a fan; its drain doesn't apply when attacking a Jace, so it's just a 1/4 flyer there.
Discard matters little in a format full of surveil, card draw, and some flashback.
Makes and pumps Cadets and keeps returning thanks to red-black's constant non-combat damage.
A strong card, and their only overlap in red's top lists.
Instant six damage that turns excess damage into Empower Jace.
A two-for-one body with a Thopter plus a late-game pump sink.
The only Way that lets planeswalkers uptick while ramping into red's strong four-drops; very powerful.
Won over by Ethan's Temur take and added it to his red top uncommons.
Solid flexible removal, either a one-damage sweep or five to one target, but less impressive than Violent Echoes.
Very good; red simply has six or seven B-level uncommons.
Two-mana deal three plus Empower Jace 1 is a very good card.
A trampling body plus a Cadet token for four, which also feeds Command the Stage.
A two-drop with first strike on your turn and a pump that make it very hard to block, and it can hold back to trade up.
Likes it, but only as a sleeper; it embarrasses most two-drops.
Green's standout common: a 4/4 trampler with flashback for another.
Worse than a five-mana 4/4 draw-a-card if the board goes badly, but its game-warping ceiling makes it green's top Jace payoff.
The mana restriction doesn't matter; it casts prepared spells and activations, and it ramps to a turn-three four-drop.
A seven-mana uncounterable 7/7 with reach, vigilance, trample, and conditional hexproof; power matches its cost.

A pushed 4/4 rate monster that draws off life gain and gives itself trample and lifelink.
Great unconditional removal plus a team pump, costed so only white-black can use it.

format.summary: Both hosts expect a deep, synergy-rich, flat-power format where no rate monsters crowd out the synergies. Empower Jace (EJ) is the defining mechanic: build either heavily around it or barely at all. Pushed double-gold uncommons incentivize finding your lane. Ben sees Jeskai (red, white, blue, black, green) and Ethan sees Temur (red, blue, green, white, black); they converge on red first and black last.
format.speed: Board presence matters: affect the board by turn two to pressure opposing Jaces and protect your own. Games snowball when one player curves out and the other durdles with land cyclers. Otherwise expect board stalls from high-toughness flying vigilance creatures.

colors.take: Clear number one for both: deep, interesting commons, pushed uncommons, and a mix of threats, burn, Empower Jace, and inherent synergy with every other color; also has the best cheap plays.
Ethan's clear second. Commons look individually weak outside Mindseeker Oculus but play better than the sum of their parts. Uncommons push toward blue-red and blue-green.
Ben ranks it high for deep commons and uncommons mixing aggression and grind, much of it resting on Blossom-Blessed Angel. Ethan ranks it fourth and finds the +1/+1 counter and life gain pieces weak.
Cares most about Empower Jace, with strong but expensive uncommons that Heartwood ramp can reach. Commons are thin beyond Bestial Incursion. Ben moved it up to third during the episode.
Last for both: excellent, splashable removal but few good threats, so it's a support color rather than a main color.

pairs.take: Ben's top archetype; prowess finally shines, with cards like Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar and Traxos.
Ben has it in his top tier alongside the red pairs; it's a surveil aggro deck with strong flyers and Surveillance Phantasm.
Top tier for Ben; non-combat damage is extremely supported via Vicious Burst, Stingerquill Voxmancer, and Grim Repriser.
Top tier; Heartwood ramp into big threats like Craftwork Crusher.
Top tier for Ben as a +1/+1 counters aggro deck; Warrior's Blades is a standout.
Ben's sleeper; the splash-the-Ways Jace deck could be oppressive or flop, and both lean toward it being good, with Kiora as a key payoff.
Ben doubts the deathtouch-plus-trample theme and ranks it bottom tier; Ethan is less skeptical, and Hapatra is a real draw.
Looks under-supported; black's weak card file worries both, though Ethan is less down on self-mill.
Middle tier; life gain and counters look supported but a bit dubious, with Bloombrute as a pushed payoff.
Middle tier; Twisted Fates is a strong reward for the pair.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Format-defining; builds a Jace token that can minus one to surveil or minus three to draw, and the Way enchantments add abilities. Temur colors best support sitting on and growing Jace, while other decks just downtick immediately.

mechanics.name: Prepare
mechanics.take: Each allied pair has a hybrid prepared spell that ties into its archetype: Peer Review makes a Cadet and surveils, Emit Variables mills, Vicious Burst deals damage, Soul Tether makes Heartwood, and Seed Suture adds a counter and gains life. The hosts call this a genius design.

mechanics.name: Heartwood tokens
mechanics.take: Effectively three-mana Manaliths tapping for red or green, with strong top end to spend the mana on and help casting heavy costs like Craftwork Crusher.

mechanics.name: Evergreen keywords
mechanics.take: Flying, vigilance, trample, prowess, and lifelink will matter a lot in the fight over Jaces; high-toughness vigilance flyers are especially strong.

advice: Prioritize two-drops and board presence so you can pressure opposing Jace tokens and protect your own; don't spend turn two land cycling.
Either commit heavily to Empower Jace or mostly ignore it; a few incidental Empower Jace cards just play as a surveil tacked on.
Respect Empower Jace in deckbuilding even when it doesn't matter every game, much like planeswalkers in War of the Spark.
Use the pushed double-gold uncommons as signals to find your lane.
Treat black as a support color for its removal rather than a main color.
Expect high-toughness flying vigilance creatures to stall boards, so value evasion, deathtouch-plus-trample, and reach.
